recommendations.rationale: Read-only phase: no parameter, production or numerical change is justified or authorized from this single execution. The unread per-update computation table and per-sample holding-window rows (see missing evidence) are needed first, because they are what would locate the tolerance-hold interval and the update at which holding tip speed stops decreasing.

The competing hypotheses concern (i) the tip-speed cost terms currently configured at zero (holding_tip_speed_weight, terminal_tip_speed_weight) and (ii) initialization-heavy, User_Requested_Stop-dominated plan selection. Testing either requires the explicit control grant for a bounded tip-speed-weight change plus a complete-execution comparison; neither is executable in this phase, and proof of a dominant cause is not required but also not available.

Do not attribute the 35 deadline misses to skipped simulated updates or to the holding-window failure: scheduling is synchronous, wall overruns inject no simulated delay, and a short projected-model probe cannot explain an entire settling failure without a complete experiment.

attribution.reason: reach_passed is true and terminal_error_m 0.007642608585867386 m is inside the displayed position_limit_m 0.01 m; the recorded failure is confined to the sampled holding window, so terminal reach is not the failed condition in this run.

The handed-over recipe displays holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 and terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 (no catalog handle for these fields in this context), while sampled terminal tip speed is 0.6351726092425104 m/s and the final-window speed maximum is 1.5810152739742807 m/s against a displayed settling speed limit of 0.02 m/s. This is a testable candidate hypothesis for residual holding tip speed, but a single execution plus configuration values do not establish cause, and no causal identification tool exists.

34 of 35 updates stop with raw status User_Requested_Stop and selected iteration 0 on the displayed rows, with recipe feasible-return budget_s 15 s and max_cpu_s 30 s against a 0.01 s control period and a handed-over mean_update_s of about 17.26 s (no catalog handle). Whether budget-limited plans explain holding behaviour cannot be established: full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained, and synchronous wall overruns do not establish skipped simulated updates.

Selection counts show 29 initialization-selected versus 6 noninitialization-selected updates with regenerate_warm_states = true, which is consistent with warm re-plans being selected rarely; but the retained record has no full warm plans or iteration traces and no closed-loop counterfactual replay, so no effect on settling or holding can be established or excluded.

Scheduling is synchronous: calls finish before fixed backend steps, and wall-clock misses do not inject simulated delay. Wall overruns therefore are not evidence of skipped simulated updates and cannot by themselves explain the observed holding-window behaviour.

facts.statement: Run-level verdicts for execution cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef: reach_passed = true with terminal_error_m = 0.007642608585867386 m at the final sampled endpoint, while joint_reach_holding_passed = false and holding_speed_passed = false, and late_max_error_m = 0.05813810428573256 m; the displayed settling criteria are position_limit_m = 0.01 m and window_s = 0.05 s. So the terminal endpoint sits inside the displayed position limit, but the enumerated late-window maximum error does not. For the recorded final holding window (six samples at 0.30, 0.31, 0.32, 0.33, 0.34, 0.35 s) the motion view reports sample counts of 6 for error_m and 6 for speed_m_s with a speed maximum of 1.5810152739742807 m/s, and the summary reports terminal_speed_m_s = 0.6351726092425104 m/s at the final sampled endpoint. Selected late-motion rows additionally report error_m 0.019054532266831993 and speed_m_s 0.7758084264853817, but their row-to-timestamp mapping is not established by the displayed catalog. Computation summary for the run: update_count = 35, stopping_counts Solve_Succeeded = 1 and User_Requested_Stop = 34, recipe max_cpu_s = 30 s and feasible-return budget_s = 15 s, regenerate_warm_states = true. Coverage: run-level summary scalars only.

On the displayed controller-update rows, plan selection reports optimization_selected_iteration = 0 for updates 7, 17, 25 and 26 and optimization_raw_status = 'User_Requested_Stop' for updates 13, 16, 17, 24 and 30; effective_horizon reads 10 control intervals for updates 6, 9 and 13, 9 for update 26 and 4 for update 31; and the run reports initialization_selected = 29 versus noninitialization_selected = 6. limitations: Every per-update observation here comes from batched derived views (updates 0-6, 7-13, 14-21, 22-29, 30-34) and the final-window motion view; no complete per-update table, no whole-trajectory ranges, no continuous-time reconstruction.

The motion view displays only the final window (6 samples, 0.30-0.35 s). The per-sample rows and the sampled backend trace over 0.01-0.29 s are retained (source.backend_motion, 35 samples) but were not displayed in this context, and this phase's two reading turns are exhausted; therefore 'where the tolerance is first met and held', 'how error/speed evolve across the run' and 'at which update speed stops decreasing' cannot be located from displayed rows alone.

The handed-over summary displays deadline_misses 35, mean_update_s 17.26331904856488 s and control_period_s 0.01 s; the displayed (truncated) fact catalogue contained no handle for these fields, so they are reported here without a fact handle.

Configured weights and scales (holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0, terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, terminal_weight 5.0, velocity_weight 0.0001, tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02, horizon 10, speed_limit_m_s 0.02) appear in the handed-over parameter block but had no displayed catalog handle; raw weight magnitudes alone would not establish cost-term importance in any case.

Full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained (control_snapshots.json absent), and no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability exists; a single execution and bounded-horizon model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause.
No derived quantities (ratios, averages, onset times, or ranges beyond the displayed ones) were computed or invented in this report.
recommended_actions: Keep this phase read-only: no execution, parameter change or numerical check is selected or authorized here.

Before any control change, acquire the per-update computation table (deadline_missed, unusable_updates, update_wall_s, optimization_status/raw_status, selected iteration, effective horizon for all 35 updates) and the per-sample holding-window rows, so the tolerance-hold interval and the speed-decrease onset can be located.

Treat the zero tip-speed cost terms and the initialization-heavy, User_Requested_Stop-dominated plan selection as competing, still-unproven hypotheses; any test of them requires the explicit control grant, a bounded candidate change and a complete-execution comparison.
